name: Auralise
description: Auralise the chosen source-receiver pairs: one anechoic sound, chosen on the Anechoic sound dropdown (a bundled recording, or a file loaded with Load...) or a File Path wired to 'sound', convolved with the impulse response of each pair. The signals keep the format of their impulse responses: mono (Simulate Mono), binaural (Simulate Binaural) or ambisonic (Simulate Ambisonics). Choose the level on the body: 'none' (default) keeps the raw level and may clip; 'relative' takes one gain from the sound convolved with every connected pair, not only the chosen ones, so the loudest connected pair would peak at -1 dBFS and a chosen pair keeps its level difference to it; 'individual' brings each signal to -1 dBFS. Save auralisation writes the signals of the chosen pairs as WAV files: choose a folder and a name (take.wav saves take_mic_<r>_<s>.wav, with r and s the receiver and source indices, as take_mic_0_0.wav, take_mic_0_1.wav, ...). Save RIR writes the impulse responses of the chosen pairs the same way, at the chosen level ('relative' from every connected response) and each with a JSON file of its metadata, including the factor back to its raw level.

inputParameters.name: irs
inputParameters.description: ImpulseResponse object(s), as Simulate gives them, one per source-receiver pair. Sources and receivers are numbered over the responses as connected, in the order they come: the n-th distinct source (receiver) is source (receiver) n, so a filtered or reordered list renumbers the pairs. The 'relative' level takes its gain from every pair connected here.

inputParameters.name: source_idx
inputParameters.description: Index or indices of the source(s) to auralise, counted over the connected responses. Dropdown: All, or 'n: name'. Empty auralises every source.

inputParameters.name: receiver_idx
inputParameters.description: Index or indices of the receiver(s) to auralise, counted over the connected responses. Dropdown: All, or 'n: name'. Empty auralises every receiver.

inputParameters.name: sound
inputParameters.description: Anechoic sound to convolve with the responses. On the Anechoic sound dropdown: one of the bundled anechoic recordings, or Load... to choose a sound file (.wav, .flac, .aiff, .ogg, .mp3), which the dropdown then lists by its name; nothing is chosen by default, and the dropdown reads '...'. A File Path connected here takes precedence. Without a sound, Auralise warns and renders nothing.

outputParameters.name: signals
outputParameters.description: One branch per chosen source-receiver pair, path {receiver;source}: the auralised signal in the format of its impulse response, shaped (samples, channels). The Audio Player plays mono (on both channels) and binaural; ambisonic signals are for saving.
